derived_from: Ahrefs Keywords Explorer, country=kr, 2026-10-05. 119 keywords recorded in ahrefs-ko-KR-market-admission-2026-10-05.json; the sixteen country pairs below are the subset where both halves were asked.
why_a_separate_file: Same reason as the tr file: the 2026-10-02 table is dated evidence for ten languages and stays byte-identical. The loader in entity_identity merges every file it is given.
rule: Unchanged: a destination country earns a language only when BOTH a connectivity keyword and a travel-information keyword carry volume in it.
the_bar_and_where_it_comes_from: The same 40 the Turkish file uses, read off what the 2026-10-02 table actually admitted (IS/de at 40, SI/it at 50). Korean clears it comfortably where Turkish barely reached it.
the_contrast_with_turkish_is_the_point: These two markets were admitted on the same day and their connectivity halves behave in opposite ways. In Turkish the eSIM intent is generic: esim nedir 5,800 and esim nasil alinir 5,100 against a per-country ceiling of 100. In Korean it is per-country and expensive: ilbon esim 2,400 at $0.30, miguk esim 600 at $0.60, yeongguk esim 200 at $0.70, dogil esim 150 at $0.70. Twelve of sixteen Korean pairs qualify, against eleven of eighteen Turkish ones that mostly scraped over the bar. A gate keyed on one market would have got one of these two badly wrong whichever market it was keyed on.
note_on_the_us: US qualifies for Korean and its four regional extracts are being captured now, so this pair becomes buildable when that finishes rather than needing anything new queued.

PT|ko.why_not: the connectivity keyword "포르투갈 esim" reads 10 a month, below the 40 that the lowest QUALIFYING pair in the 2026-10-02 table was admitted on. The travel half is real here - "포르투갈 여행" 1,600 - and one half is not enough. Portugal is the clearest case of the asymmetry the rule exists to catch: 1,600 a month reading about it and 10 a month wanting a SIM for it.
